correctness.rationale: All faces are exhaustively classified for arbitrary m: the only new faces on edge deletion are one full tetrahedron and 2m-4 triangles. The old complex is a graph K_m with binom(m,2) tetrahedral spheres attached along contractible trees. The added three-simplex kills the primitive S_12 sphere; first triangles attach along m-2 primitive independent graph loops, second triangles along homotopic loops and produce m-2 explicit new two-spheres. This gives integral kernels, images and cokernels, all with unit coefficients. Direct subset enumeration m=2..6 and exact signed boundary identities, plus mod 2, 3, 5 chain ranks, corroborate but do not substitute for uniform proof.

value.rationale: The cocktail-party family is a standard strongly regular multipartite family; edge deletion is its minimal nontrivial symmetry-breaking fault. The claim computes actual, primitive integral persistence under that mutation in two simultaneous homological dimensions, including explicit geometric generators of all killed and born classes. This map-level information is not determined by prior absolute homotopy classifications and is a natural benchmark for topological stability under graph faults.
